newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks slightly up as market awaits summit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks slightly up as market awaits summit.

text.p: Israeli shares closed with a positive bias in dull trading on Wednesday as investors awaited the outcome of the Middle East summit in Washington which was called to end the latest Palestinian-Israeli violence.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.17 percent, or 0.32 points, to 184.41. The Maof 25 index gained 0.27 percent to 194.02.
"Investors are in a waiting pattern and activity was dull and mixed. We are all waiting for the results of the Washington summit," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House.
"Investors are a little bit more optimistic but they are also very cautious. Overall today's rise is meaningless because the market rose on a very low volume," Weisberg said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton called for a two-day summit to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palesinians. Five days of clashes that killed 72 people erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
"The market is dead, many shares were not traded and activity is very low. Investors are more optimistic but the market will not recover in the near future," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
"Investors are waiting for the results of the Middle East summit but nobody expects a real breakthrough," he said.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.25 percent to 142,879 on turnover of 3.8 million shekels; Koor Industries, which gained 0.5 percent to 28,238 on turnover of 3.0 million shekels; and Super Sol, which closed unchanged at 7,300 on volume of 1.8 million shekels.
The Tel Aviv bourse will close two hours early throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth. Normal trading hours will resume on October 6.
